steps: Reading ops.facility in the operations data: 13 facilities, 3 business codes
Looking for collection routes, transfer stations and municipal landfills
msw.none: No municipal waste operations in the connected data. Ironbridge treats, incinerates, recycles and disposes of regulated waste from industrial generators. A municipal collection company would bring its own routes, transfer stations and tonnage contracts; connect its systems first, or pick Hazardous waste management.

roles.name: Waste Stream Analyst
roles.blurb: Characterises new waste streams, finds the unit in the network that can take each one under its permit, its capacity and the customer requirement, prices it on full cost against the floors, and keeps every accepted stream with an outlet.

areas.name: Characterise and classify
areas.what: Reads each new profile against its released results, the codes and the treatment standard, and says what the stream is before anyone prices it.
tasks: Check the profile against released laboratory results and flag what the generator did not say
Assign federal, state and land disposal codes and the treatment standard
Read customer requirements that bind the routing
Return incomplete profiles to the generator with the questions
Keep approved profiles current before they expire

areas.name: Size the exposure
areas.what: Puts a number on what a stream, a contract or an event is worth and what it puts at risk.
tasks: Size tons a year and revenue a year for each new generator
Size what an outage, an expiring approval or a permit decision strands
Track the revenue riding on profiles that expire in 90 days

areas.name: Route in the network
areas.what: Finds the unit that can take a stream under its permit, its capacity in the period and the customer requirement, and names the fallback.
tasks: Match each stream to the permitted units and rule out the ones without capacity in the period
Name the alternative unit and the third-party outlet for every stream
Check halogen, mercury and reactive limits before fuel blending or the kiln
Keep the ten-day transfer clock at the service centers

areas.name: Price the economics
areas.what: Costs every route on full cost and prices the stream from the book against the floors.
tasks: Cost treatment, handling, transport and the state fee on the route the stream will take
Price from the 2026 book and test the 28% contract floor and the 15% stream floor
Re-price when a fee rises and check the pass-through clause
Compare quotes with the book and explain the exceptions

areas.name: Keep watching
areas.what: Checks every nightly load so a stream never loses its outlet or falls under the floor without someone knowing.
tasks: Check manifests, bookings, approvals and the price book after every 02:00 load
Look across the network before a third-party outlet is booked
Flag approvals and permits coming up for decision

areas.name: Submissions
areas.what: Turns the above into the acceptance memo, the quote, the pricing schedule, the re-route notice and the committee paper.
tasks: Draft the acceptance memo and the quote letter for each new generator
Build the pricing schedule in the approved structure
Draft the re-route notice when shipments lose their outlet
Prepare the quarterly Capacity Committee pack

questions.q: Which profiles are pending approval, and which of them are waiting on a laboratory result?

answer.text: 269 profiles are pending approval; 265 of them have no released laboratory result and cannot be approved yet. Halden Biopharma's six are pending with results released on 29 October: they wait on the quote and the acceptance memo, not on the laboratory.
sources: ops.waste_profile · Status Pending with receipt dates

questions.q: Which Halden streams carry a laboratory finding the profile did not say?

answer.figLabel: the solvent: 3.2% halogens the profile did not say
answer.text: One. H2 methanol and DMSO solvent: total halogens 3.2% by weight from a chlorinated intermediate the profile did not mention, above Fox Hollow's 2.0% fuel blending limit. The other five results match the profiles: H1 is not ignitable with 40 mg/L active ingredient, H6 is pH 12.6 (D002 as profiled).
sources: ops.profile_analytical · Released results for the Halden profiles

questions.q: How long does a profile take from receipt to approval?

answer.text: A profile takes a median of 9 days from receipt to approval this year (90th percentile 23 days); the laboratory release is 5 days of it. Pharmaceutical and lab pack profiles take longest because the chemist asks for a second sample more often.

questions.q: Which approved profiles expire in the next 90 days, and what revenue rides on them?

answer.text: 458 approved profiles expire in the next 90 days, $34.5M of annual revenue at their current prices and tons. Each needs a renewed characterisation and, where the laboratory asks, a fresh result before the expiry date.
sources: ops.waste_profile · Approved profiles with expiry, tons and price

questions.q: What does the Port Terrell outage strand, and where can each shipment go?

answer.text: The outage strands 14 inbound shipments, 911 tons and $0.71M of revenue, booked for Port Terrell over the next two weeks. 11 can go to Granger within its headroom, 1 organic-liquid load to Northstar Thermal, 2 can wait on the pad at Galena Shores inside the ten-day clock, and 2 arrive after the restart and stay booked. Extra cost $61k.
sources: ops.manifest · Open manifests booked for Port Terrell
ops.capacity_booking · Outage weeks and Granger headroom
ops.transfer_hold · Galena Shores holds and deadlines

questions.q: What does the 1 November fee rise do to margin, and which contracts carry the pass-through clause?

answer.text: The Texas fee rose $2.50 a ton and the Illinois fee $3.00 on 1 November. At the last three months' pace that is about $39,515 a month at Port Terrell, Bayou Verde and Galena Shores and $49,248 at Riverbend. Contracts with clause 9.2 pass it through from the next invoice; two Riverbend stabilization contracts carry no clause and fell under the stream floor.
sources: fin.state_fee · Fees before and from 1 November
ops.manifest · Received tons by state, August to October

answer.text: 3 units are booked above 90% of their fourth-quarter capacity, all three at Port Terrell: aqueous incineration 94.4%, organic liquids 94.9%, solids 93.0%. The next tightest is Granger organic liquids at 86.1%.

ops.process_unit · Permitted tons a year by unit

questions.q: What is booked against the capacity of each incineration unit, and what headroom is left in November?

answer.text: Granger is booked at 70.9% on aqueous incineration and 86.1% on organic liquids for the quarter; in weeks 45 and 46 it has 336 tons of aqueous, 217 of solids and 91 of organic liquids free. Port Terrell has no headroom in those weeks: the kiln is down.
sources: ops.capacity_booking · Booked and capacity by unit and week

questions.q: Which units could take each of the six Halden streams under their permits?

answer.figLabel: each with at least one permitted unit; three with two
answer.text: Every Halden stream has at least one permitted unit that meets its requirement. H1 process wastewater: Granger or Port Terrell aqueous incineration (deep well is permitted but is disposal; aqueous treatment is not an outlet for the active ingredient). H2 solvent: incineration at Granger or Port Terrell; Fox Hollow is ruled out by halogens and Tidewater is permitted but under renewal. H3 lab packs: Granger. H4 aerosols: Cypress Landing. H5 solids: Granger or Port Terrell. H6 scrubber water: Bayou Verde deep well, Riverbend, Newbury Works or Bayou Verde aqueous treatment.
sources: Halden_Quality_Requirement_QR-14_Waste_Destruction.pdf · Destruction with a certificate; deep well and landfill not acceptable

questions.q: Which shipments are on the pad at Galena Shores today, and when does each one's clock run out?

answer.figLabel: loads on the pad at Galena Shores; 4 must move on
answer.text: 6 Port Terrell loads are on the pad at Galena Shores. The first runs out of clock on 11 November 2026; 4 of them run out before the kiln is back on 15 November and have to move on, 2 can wait.
sources: ops.transfer_hold · Arrival and deadline per hold
ops.manifest · The loads and their units
Mailbox · Jenna Fairbanks · Coordinator: the first two run out before the kiln is back

questions.q: Is the Halden solvent waste acceptable at Fox Hollow for fuel blending?

answer.text: No. The released result puts total halogens at 3.2% by weight, above Fox Hollow's 2.0% fuel blending limit; the codes (D001, F003, U154) are permitted there, the material is not. Tidewater's limit is 5.0% and the route is permitted, but it earns 5.8% from Texas and the permit is under renewal. The stream is quoted as organic-liquid incineration at Granger.

questions.q: What would the six Halden streams earn a year by route, at the price book, on full cost?

answer.text: At the price book on full cost the six streams earn $3.56M a year with $1.24M of margin (34.7%) on the recommended routing: the three QR-14 streams incinerated at Granger, aerosols at Cypress Landing, scrubber water to Bayou Verde deep well. Quoted on Port Terrell the margin would be 43.0%, on capacity that is 94% booked and not planned for 2027.

questions.q: Which approved profiles are under the 15% stream floor at today's fees?

answer.figLabel: Below the stream floor · of 2597 approved
answer.text: 2 approved profiles earn less than the 15.0% stream floor at the approved route and today's fees, 2 of them stabilization at Riverbend after the Illinois fee rose on 1 November. Legacy profiles are not counted: their prices are the acquired companies' books.
sources: ops.waste_profile · Approved profiles with price, route and origin
fin.treatment_cost · Treatment cost a ton by unit

questions.q: Which quotes this year were priced below the price book, and by how much?

answer.text: 127 quote lines on 99 quotes were priced below the 2026 price book, $434,424 a year of discount at the quoted tons. The deepest is 10.0%, above the 5% that needs the Pricing and Margin Manager.
sources: fin.quote_line · Quoted and book price per line

questions.q: What does a re-route from Port Terrell to Granger cost a ton on the rate card, by origin region?

answer.figLabel: aqueous liquids from the Gulf origin region
answer.text: From the Gulf origin region a re-route from Port Terrell to Granger adds $67.66 a ton on aqueous liquids: the haul grows from 140 to 1020 miles, Granger's treatment cost is $5 lower, and the Indiana fee is 50 cents above the Texas fee from 1 November.
sources: fin.transport_lane · Rates by origin region and facility

questions.q: Which third-party approvals expire in the next 60 days, and which streams depend on them?

answer.figLabel: Expiring in 60 days · all Meridian West
answer.text: 38 third-party approvals expire by 2 January, all at Meridian West on 30 November. Two are the Gulf overflow profiles (Delmar Chemical, Gulf Coast Coatings) that carry Port Terrell solids this autumn; the rest are West Coast profiles with no other outlet. Granger is permitted for the two overflow profiles and costs less.
sources: ops.waste_profile · The profiles and their generators

questions.q: Which permits and outlet approvals come up for decision in the next 90 days?

answer.figLabel: decisions in 90 days: Tidewater renewal, Meridian West approvals
answer.text: Two. Tidewater's fuel blending permit renewal: decision due 18 December, no new three-year volume there without a fallback until then. The Meridian West approvals on the two Gulf overflow profiles: expire 30 November, renewal at the 2027 price with re-approval. Pacific Reach Environmental's audit is pending and it is not an outlet.

questions.q: What did we invoice this year by business, against the plan, and at what margin?

answer.text: $192.3M was invoiced January to September against $198.2M planned for those months, 3.0% under, at 37.5% margin on full cost. Gulf is the only business above its plan; East is furthest under.
sources: fin.invoice_line · Invoiced revenue and full cost of shipments received January to September 2026
fin.revenue_plan · FY26 plan by business and month
ops.facility · Business of each receiving facility

questions.q: How many Harbor Line and Tidewater profiles are still on the legacy system, and how many has a chemist reviewed?

answer.text: 578 profiles are still on LegacyTrack: 348 from Harbor Line and 230 from Tidewater. None has been reviewed by an Approval Chemist; they are read into the graph marked legacy and are not counted as approved Ironbridge profiles. Migration starts in January, Newbury Works first.
sources: legacy.legacy_profile · Profiles with source company and reviewed flag

questions.q: What does Priya need for the Halden proposal by Friday, and what is ready?

answer.text: By Friday 6 November: a price per ton for each of the six streams, the facility each goes to, the capacity held and the fallback, in the Delmar pricing schedule structure, with the acceptance memo for Dana and Marcus. Ready: the six profiles, the released results, the permits and the fourth-quarter bookings. Open: the quote itself (draft Q-2026-0141), the first-quarter plan from Port Terrell, and Halden's EPA identification number.
sources: Mailbox · Priya Natarajan · Account manager: quote by Friday in the Delmar structure
